takeaway: Hematopoietic progenitors bifurcate sharply at t* = 0.44 along an antagonistic GATA1–SPI1 switch whose perturbation reverses erythroid versus myeloid lineage bias.
caption: Synthetic single-cell CRISPRi perturbation and hematopoietic lineage bifurcation atlas (Cell Press double column, 174.0 mm). (A) Two-dimensional developmental landscape with velocity stream lines showing progenitor bifurcation into erythroid and myeloid fates at commitment pseudotime t* = 0.44. (B) Pseudotime-ordered expression cascade of ten lineage transcription factors (z-scored). (C) CRISPRi knockdown log-odds shift toward erythroid versus myeloid fate (mean and 95% CI). (D) Opposing dynamics of GATA1 and SPI1 across pseudotime with single-cell scatter and smooth 95% confidence ribbons. All data are synthetic.
label: fig:cell_lineage_bifurcation

panels.note: RNA velocity stream lines split progenitors cleanly into erythroid (upper) and myeloid (lower) branches.
Ten master regulators wave sequentially along pseudotime, diverging cleanly past the t* = 0.44 rail.
GATA1/KLF1 knockdown depletes erythroid fate (-1.9 to -1.3 log-odds) whereas SPI1/IRF8 knockdown enriches it.
GATA1 and SPI1 trajectories cross precisely at t* = 0.44 before locking into mutually exclusive states.
